helpIntro: Michigan State uses numerical grades from 4.0 to 0.0 in 0.5 steps. Enter semester credits and final MSU numerical grades to estimate your current and projected GPA.
helpNote: For the standard undergraduate institutional GPA. MSU truncates official GPA to three decimals. CR/NC and P/N grades are excluded, external transfer grades do not enter MSU GPA, and professional-school records such as Law need separate rules.
helpExample: A 3-credit 4.0 earns 12 grade points; a 3-credit 3.0 earns 9. Together, 21 ÷ 6 = 3.500.

gradeExplanations.4.0: 4.0 counts in GPA at 4 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.3.5: 3.5 counts in GPA at 3.5 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.3.0: 3.0 counts in GPA at 3 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.2.5: 2.5 counts in GPA at 2.5 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.2.0: 2.0 counts in GPA at 2 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.1.5: 1.5 counts in GPA at 1.5 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.1.0: 1.0 counts in GPA at 1 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.0.0: 0.0 counts in GPA at 0 points per credit.
gradeExplanations.NS: Pandemic-era Not Satisfactory; excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete; excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.V: Visitor; non-credit and excluded from GPA.

specialTypes.name: MSU course, undergraduate numerical grading
specialTypes.note: Use for finalized MSU numerical grades.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: Accepted external credit does not enter MSU term or cumulative GPA.

specialTypes.name: College of Law or other professional grading system
specialTypes.note: Do not apply the undergraduate numerical scale to a professional-school record.

repeatPolicy.note: For an eligible repeat, the last grade and credits replace the previous grade in cumulative GPA. Confirm repeat eligibility and limits with MSU.
